title: Undefined Behavior in Concurrency and Signal Safety
platform_conditions: C11 memory model and POSIX signal semantics (Linux, macOS); specific manifestations depend on compiler optimization and CPU memory ordering
security_mechanism: Signed arithmetic overflow is undefined behavior, so a bounds check like `if (len + offset < len)` written with signed ints can be deleted by the optimizer, which assumes the condition cannot be true. Unsynchronized access to the same object from two threads is a data race and again undefined behavior: without atomics or a mutex, one thread's write may become visible torn, reordered, or never — so a credentials or configuration flag checked without synchronization can appear set in one thread while another still observes it unset. Signal handlers add reentrancy: the handler runs on the same thread at an arbitrary point, so calling malloc/printf (non-async-signal-safe, both take internal locks) can deadlock or corrupt the heap when the signal arrives mid-allocation.

source_sink_clues.source: Attacker-controlled magnitudes that overflow signed arithmetic on validation paths, concurrent requests hitting shared state, and signals an adversary can trigger (SIGSEGV via malformed input, timers, SIGINT on exposed service processes).
source_sink_clues.sink: Signed overflow arithmetic guarding security checks; reads/writes of shared flags or pointers without atomics or locks; printf/malloc/memcpy and other non-async-signal-safe calls inside signal handlers

tracking_guards: Check that overflow-sensitive bounds arithmetic uses unsigned types or checked builtins (__builtin_add_overflow) before the comparison, that shared security state is _Atomic or mutex-protected, and that signal handlers restrict themselves to volatile sig_atomic_t flags or write() on a self-pipe.
not_candidate_when: The arithmetic is unsigned with wrapping treated explicitly, the shared state is confined to one thread or already synchronized, the handler only sets a sig_atomic_t flag, or the concurrency is unreachable from request paths (single-threaded build, init-only state).
public_references: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/362.html
CWE-479: Signal Handler Use of a Non-reentrant Function — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/479.html
SEI CERT C Coding Standard: SIG30-C (async-signal-safe handlers), MSC21-C (UB in checks)
